html:
Kamerun was a colony of Germany in central Africa from 1884 to 1916, covering what is now Cameroon and parts of its neighbours. The map shows it in 1914.

In 1884 the Duala chiefs of the coast signed a treaty that Germany treated as a protectorate. German forces then pushed inland against stiff resistance, and companies set up plantations on the slopes of Mount Cameroon. In 1911, after a crisis with France over Morocco, Germany gained a large strip of French Equatorial Africa. In 1914 the Germans hanged the Duala king Rudolf Duala Manga Bell, who had protested against the seizure of his people's land.

In World War I British, French and Belgian forces invaded. By early 1916 the last German troops had crossed into neutral Spanish Guinea. The League of Nations then split Kamerun into French Cameroun and British Cameroons, whose southern part is the map's Southern Cameroon.
sum: Kamerun was a colony of Germany in central Africa from 1884 to 1916, covering what is now Cameroon and parts of its neighbours. The map shows it in 1914.
